text: It's actually raining, so for once I get to play this and look clever. The Cult, Rain. [dryly] Gerrit's gone into his crate. Some seabird.
Hardly rain at all out there, more a damp rumour on the glass. The Cult would want more than this. Rain, while we wait for the real thing.
Not a drop. Clear sky, dry deck, and I'm playing Rain by The Cult anyway, in case anyone up there takes requests.
Dark everywhere except the lighthouse, going round and round. Soundgarden, Black Hole Sun. [quietly] Some songs belong to this hour.
Middle of the afternoon and the sky's gone the colour of a bruise. Black Hole Sun, Soundgarden. They knew.
The sun's so bright off the water I've got my sunglasses on in the wheelhouse. Soundgarden, Black Hole Sun, to take the edge off.
The sun's been in and out of the clouds all afternoon, like it can't make up its mind. Red Hot Chili Peppers, Behind The Sun.
No sun anywhere, just fog, thick as wool round the wheelhouse. Somewhere above it, it's shining. Behind The Sun, by the Red Hot Chili Peppers.
The sun's getting low behind the island and the lighthouse is warming up to take over. Red Hot Chili Peppers. Behind The Sun.
Flat water, clear sky, the Zeemeeuw barely moving on her chain. For once the title tells the truth. Queens of the Stone Age, Smooth Sailing.
[deadpan] The deck's at an angle, the kettle's in the sink for its own safety, and the next song is Smooth Sailing. Queens of the Stone Age. Call it hope.
Gusts coming round the point hard enough that Gerrit just flew past the window backwards. This one's for him. Smooth Sailing, Queens of the Stone Age.
Paolo Nutini, Iron Sky. Look out of any window and you'll see why: low, grey, and leaning on the sea. Opa's coughing. [quietly] Hold on, old man.
A lid on the whole sea all evening, grey on grey, the lamp on early. If there's a song for an evening like this, it's Iron Sky. Paolo Nutini.
Not one gap in the clouds since breakfast. An iron sky, all afternoon long, and Paolo Nutini gave it a song.
Clear night. From the deck you can see every star there is, with the lighthouse beam sweeping underneath. Elton John, Rocket Man. [wistful] The second loneliest job going.
Early. The coffee hasn't done a thing yet, and I think it's going to be a long, long time before it does. Rocket Man, Elton John.
Sterrenstof means stardust, and there's a whole sky of the real thing over the boat tonight. De Jeugd Van Tegenwoordig.
First stars coming out over the lighthouse, and I haven't even had supper. De Jeugd Van Tegenwoordig, with Sterrenstof. [fondly] Stardust, for the cold months.
Out here at this hour there are two lights I trust: the lighthouse, going round, and the lamp on my mast, staying put. The Black Keys, Everlasting Light.
The fog's so thick the lighthouse is just a smudge going round. Everlasting Light, The Black Keys, for the keeper up there doing the actual work.
Pitch dark past the bow, and nothing out there but a wave now and then catching the beam. Royal Blood, Out of the Black. Loud, to keep the dark honest.
Sea, sky, island... all one colour at this hour. The Rolling Stones got there first. Paint It Black.
Dark by supper this time of year, and the lamp goes on before the kettle does. Paint It Black, The Rolling Stones.
Morning. Last night was the usual: one gull, one generator, one DJ, and nobody dancing. The Strokes. Last Nite.
First coffee, the burner hissing, Gerrit blinking at me from his crate. It takes us both a while to come together. The Beatles.
Coffee's not working yet. [mutters] Maybe this will. Oasis, Supersonic.
Some might say it'll clear up by lunch. [dryly] Gerrit says it won't, and he's been out in it. Oasis, Some Might Say, while we find out.
Warm enough for swimmers off the island's beach. Mind the current round the point, it's stronger than it looks. Vance Joy, Riptide.
Hot enough to fry an egg on the wheelhouse roof. Gerrit tried it with a fish. [deadpan] He ate it anyway. Django Django, Life's a Beach.
Snow on the island's beach. I didn't know that was allowed. Django Django, Life's a Beach, said with a straight face.
Snow on the deck, and I'm playing a song from the other side of the world, where somebody's probably in shorts. Men At Work, Down Under. [sighs] Good for them.
Morning here, which means on the other side of the world they're putting the kettle on for supper. Men At Work, Down Under.
Rain on the roof, one lamp on, and the slowest blues in the box. Red House, Jimi Hendrix.
A soft grey drizzle, nothing in a hurry, not even the clouds. Jack Johnson's Breakdown is about the right speed for it.
Warm afternoon, hatch open, feet up on the console. Jack Johnson, They Do, They Don't. [warmly] Lovely.
Fog. The ferry's horn somewhere off to the left, Opa to the right, and me in the middle. The Cars, Moving in Stereo.
Evening, fish in the pan, and the first song with brass in it. Coleen. The Heavy and the Dap-Kings Horns.
Sleet. Not rain, not snow, just the sky being rude. Beatsteaks, then, short and loud. Cheap Comments.
The wind's pushing Gerrit round the sky like a paper bag. [deadpan] He has a tail and still can't steer. Queens of the Stone Age, If I Had A Tail.
A warm evening, every hatch open, the island's lights coming on one by one. Make It Wit Chu, Queens of the Stone Age.
Snow on the wheelhouse glass and my toes gave up an hour ago. Jon Fratelli, Santo Domingo. A man can dream.
Raining, and Gerrit's folded himself into his crate like a dog in a bag. The Fratellis. Doginabag.
Still here. Most DJs roll over and go to bed about now. [dryly] Most DJs have a bed that doesn't move. Jet, Rollover D.J.
Sun on the water, first coffee, and Opa running like a dream. I'll praise all three. Fatboy Slim, Praise You.
The ferry went past in this fog a minute ago. Heard her horn, never saw her. The Black Keys, She's Long Gone.
Just me and the anchor light at this hour. Gerrit's asleep with his head under his wing. Lonely Boy, The Black Keys, and I'm not complaining.
In fog like this you can hear the buoy bells all the way from the harbour mouth. A Bell Will Ring. Oasis.
Hail on the roof like somebody emptying a bag of marbles. Franz Ferdinand. Bullet. [flatly] Appropriate.
Middle of the afternoon and the wheelhouse is dark as a cinema, the clouds are that low. Franz Ferdinand, The Dark Of The Matinée.
Lovely evening. If anyone wants to take me out, I'm the trawler with the gull on the aerial. Franz Ferdinand, Take Me Out. Nobody's offered yet.
Autumn, and the trees on the island are dropping everything they've got. A few leaves even made it out to the deck. The Fallen, by Franz Ferdinand.
The badger's out on the island about now, I'd bet, doing his rounds while everyone sleeps. Franz Ferdinand, Treason! Animals.
Cold morning, gloves on at the desk. I can still feel my fingers, which is good news. Franz Ferdinand, Can't Stop Feeling.
Every window open and not one breath of air coming through any of them. Black Pistol Fire. Suffocation Blues. [sighs] Weather report, basically.
The light's gone orange and red over the island, the sea's copying it. Charles Bradley, with the Menahan Street Band. The World Is Going Up In Flames.
Sun bouncing off the water and onto the wheelhouse ceiling in little gold ripples. The Black Keys took the words out of my mouth. Gold on the Ceiling.
In fog like this I could tell you we're anchored off San Francisco and you couldn't prove otherwise. Arctic Monkeys, Fake Tales Of San Francisco. [amused] Close enough.
Grey sky, flat sea, not warm, not cold, nothing happening. Kaiser Chiefs, Everything Is Average Nowadays. [flatly] The forecast, set to music.
Up at all hours, pale, not keen on daylight. Gerrit has his suspicions about me. Arctic Monkeys, Perhaps Vampires Is A Bit Strong But.
Evening. On the mainland, people are getting ready to go out dancing. [mock-serious] I've put on the clean jumper. Arctic Monkeys, I Bet You Look Good On The Dancefloor.
With the deck moving like this, I'm dancing whether I like it or not. Might as well have a song. Mando Diao, Dance With Somebody.
Grey drizzle, the lighthouse gone blurry... [quietly] nothing wrong, exactly. Mando Diao, Maybe Just Sad.
Lightning over the mainland, and every flash I check the aerial. Gerrit's off it, for once. [to Gerrit] Wise bird. The Strokes, Electricityscape.
Spring, and the path round the island's busy with walkers again. I watch them through the binoculars, [wistful] all of them in better shoes than me. The Walker, Fitz and The Tantrums.
Lovely day for a walk, I'm told, by people who can walk further than nine steps in a straight line. Fitz and The Tantrums. The Walker.
Somewhere it's warm. [flatly] Not here. Slash and Myles Kennedy, Back from Cali, for anyone else with two jumpers on.
A clear morning out here feels like a promise somebody actually kept. Slash, with Chris Cornell. Promise.
Rain running down the wheelhouse windows in little rivers, every one taking its own way down. Velvet Revolver, Slither.
Quiet night. The swell comes in, breaks on the island's rocks, and falls to pieces. [quietly] Over and over. Velvet Revolver, Fall to Pieces.
Morning medication: coffee, black, from the one mug. Queens of the Stone Age, Medication, and a second cup after.
Where the ferry is right now, no one knows. [under his breath] Not even her captain, in fog like this. Queens of the Stone Age. No One Knows.
Everyone asleep, the island dark, and the only voice on the water is this one. God Is In The Radio, Queens of the Stone Age. [dryly] I'm only the bloke who fixes it.
Snow coming down on the sea without a sound, the whole bay gone quiet as a church. Hozier, Take Me To Church.
Summer. There are raspberries on the island, I'm told, along the path behind the lighthouse. I get the song instead. The Birds of Satan, Raspberries.
Sleet coming sideways at the wheelhouse door. You Can Be So Cruel, Royal Blood. [mutters] I'm talking to the sky.
Dark when I get up this time of year, and dark when the coffee's done. Ben Howard, Keep Your Head Up.
Grey sky pressing down on everything all day. Don't let it get you down. Nor the man. Fatboy Slim.
The sun's just breaking through, one long stripe across the water to the island. The Doors, Break On Through.
A sky full of stars, and Gerrit asleep under every one of them. Just Jack, Starz In Their Eyes.
Too hot to think in this wheelhouse. Alice In Chains, Check My Brain. [exhales] I'd check mine, but it's melted.
Flat calm, and the lighthouse beam keeps catching something out on the water. A seal, I'd say. [amused] Probably. The Black Hollies, Eyes Of Mermaide.
The Zeemeeuw won't sit still on her chain in this wind. Alle Farben and Graham Candy have a song about it. She Moves.
This late, the island's all vampires and wolves. [clears throat] Well. One badger and an owl. The Wombats, Tokyo.
The swell's up, my coffee's on the floor, [sighs] and the chart table's made a run for it. We Were Promised Jetpacks, Peaks and Troughs.
No shade on a trawler. None. The Black Keys, Gotta Get Away, and I'm going nowhere but the shady side of the wheelhouse.
The fog's crept closer all evening, and now it's sitting on the bow. Kings of Leon, Closer.
Waves against the hull, wind against the wheelhouse, [dryly] Opa against both. Kings of Leon, Beautiful War.
Story time, for anyone still awake. The Fratellis, A Heady Tale. Gerrit's gone to sleep already. [dryly] He's heard it.
Fish in the pan, Gerrit at the window looking innocent, and Henrietta on the turntable. The Fratellis.
A cold evening, the stove ticking, both hands round the mug. George Ezra, Budapest.
Evening, lamp on, and the sea calm enough to dance on. [amused] For a change. The Wombats, Let's Dance to Joy Division.
The daylight ran out hours ago. [deadpan] The coffee hasn't. OneRepublic, Love Runs Out.
Grey again. Out here that's the factory setting. Django Django, Default.
Morning, Gerrit. [sighs] Yes, yes, a fish, I know. Sam Means has a song for you. Yeah Yeah.
Something loud for the late watch, to keep Opa company. Foo Fighters, Hey, Johnny Park!
Late, and dark, and the right hour for it. The Rolling Stones, remixed by The Neptunes. Sympathy For The Devil.
Thunder rolling round the bay, and Wolfmother trying to out-shout it. Joker And The Thief.
Rain on the wheelhouse roof, the lamp swinging a little, and Jimi Hendrix. Hey Joe.
Sunshine, then hail, then sunshine again, all inside ten minutes. Crazy, Gnarls Barkley. I'd say it's the weather.
Calm, clear, warm, Opa purring. On a day like this I'm a fortunate son. [dryly] Creedence Clearwater Revival would put it differently.
Wind strong enough to knock a man down on the foredeck, so I'm staying in. Red Hot Chili Peppers, Knock Me Down.
Opa doesn't like starting in the cold. I sing him Wolfmother to warm him up. Woman. [mutters] He's still deciding.
Rainy evening, the kind for sorting things out. The Birds of Satan, Pieces of the Puzzle.
Bright morning, and Opa's running, so everything's around the bend in a good way. The Asteroids Galaxy Tour, Around The Bend.
Long winter dark, and every window on the island lit. This one's for whoever's on their own tonight. [warmly] Not alone, then. The Fratellis, My Friend John.
Fog thick enough to lean on, and the lighthouse beam playing tricks in it: there, gone, there. Fatboy Slim, The Joker.
Summer evening, still light, and somewhere on the island a party's starting. Franz Ferdinand, No You Girls.
Showers coming and going all morning, one after the other like little sisters. Queens of the Stone Age, Little Sister.
Hail. The sky's in an argument and it's winning. Fiction Plane, Soldier Machismo.
Rain drumming on the roof in perfect time, and I still can't dance. Jon Fratelli has a song about that. Rhythm Doesn't Make You A Dancer.
Mackerel running in the warm water, a bucket of them on deck, and Gerrit's already helped himself. I Got Mine, The Black Keys.
Spring, the days getting longer, and Opa sounding like he's been drinking coffee too. Foster The People, Pumped Up Kicks.
Autumn gives with one hand, all that colour on the island, and takes with the other, the light. Queens of the Stone Age, First It Giveth.
Snow coming down, every flake taking its own way to the water. The Kooks, She Moves In Her Own Way.
